newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BNZ raises NZ fixed rates but holds variable-NZPA.
newsitem.headline: BNZ raises NZ fixed rates but holds variable-NZPA.

text.p: The Bank of New Zealand told the New Zealand Press Association on Thursday it was raising its fixed mortgage rates for homeowners and business but it was sticking to a previously announced cut in its variable mortgage rate.

On Wednesday, Countrywide Bank announced it was raising its variable mortgage rate to 10.5 percent from 8.95 percent in response to a sharp rise in interest rates on the wholesale money market last week.
Countrywide's move has raised speculation that other banks will either cancel previously announced cuts in their variable rates or raise them to a similar level.

BNZ spokesman Rowan McArthur said that the BNZ had decided not to change its previously announced decision to cut its variable mortgage rate to 8.95 percent from 9.40 percent from August 4 but the decision would be reviewed again on August 4.

However, the bank has raised its one-year fixed mortgage lending rate to 9.25 percent from 8.10 percent, its two-year rate to 9.25 percent from 8.60 percent and its three-year rate to 8.95 percent from 8.60 percent effective from next Monday.
For business lending, the one-year fixed rate will be raised to 9.5 percent from 8.5 percent, two-year to 9.5 percent from 8.75 percent and three-year to 9.25 percent from 8.75 percent.
The four- and five-year rate will be raised to 9.25 percent from 8.95 percent.
McArthur said the BNZ would review the variable rate again on August 4.
"It will all depend on the movements at that point," he said.
He declined to comment on the 10.5 percent variable rate set by Countrywide but said the situation was volatile and confusing to customers.
Countrywide managing director David Wolfenden said the increase in his bank's variable rate was the result of the rising cost of wholesale funds.
The 90-day bank bill rate, off which many mortgage products are priced, was at 8.56 percent this morning, unchanged from Wednesday but up from 7.70 percent a week ago.
Variable mortgage rates are typically priced between one and two percent above the 90-day bill rate.

The bank-bill rate has risen to offset the fall in the kiwi dollar in the last week. This has meant that monetary conditions, which are a mix of the two, have remained little changed overall, while the mix of the conditions has altered radically.
